categories.blurbEn: Greetings, courtesy, days of the week, and the basic question words you'll use every day.

entries.note: gendered — a man says obrigado, a woman says obrigada

entries.replyPt: Estou bem, obrigado. E tu?
entries.replyEn: I'm well, thanks. And you?

entries.replyPt: De nada, foi um prazer.
entries.replyEn: You're welcome, it was a pleasure.

entries.en: Sorry, I didn't understand. Can you repeat that?
entries.replyPt: Claro, sem problema.
entries.replyEn: Sure, no problem.

entries.en: Excuse me, can I get by?
entries.replyPt: Força, claro.
entries.replyEn: Go ahead, of course.

entries.replyPt: Hoje é quarta-feira.
entries.replyEn: Today is Wednesday.

entries.pt: Onde fica a casa de banho?
entries.replyPt: É ali à direita, depois da cozinha.
entries.replyEn: It's over there on the right, past the kitchen.
entries.note: casa de banho — in Brazil: o banheiro

categories.blurbEn: The everyday routine — waking up, getting ready, breakfast, and telling the time.

entries.note: in Brazil: o café da manhã
reflexive verb — levanto-me, levantas-te, levanta-se
in Brazil: tomar banho

entries.en: What time do you wake up?
entries.replyPt: Acordo às sete e meia.
entries.replyEn: I wake up at half past seven.

entries.pt: Já são horas de te levantares!
entries.replyPt: Já vou, espera só um bocadinho.
entries.replyEn: I'm coming, just wait a moment.

entries.replyPt: São oito em ponto.
entries.replyEn: It's eight o'clock sharp.

entries.replyPt: É lá para as oito e um quarto.
entries.replyEn: It's around a quarter past eight.

entries.en: Do you shower in the morning or at night?
entries.replyPt: De manhã, para acordar melhor.
entries.replyEn: In the morning, to wake up properly.

entries.en: Are you going to bed early today?
entries.replyPt: Vou, estou cansada.
entries.replyEn: I am, I'm tired.

entries.replyPt: Já, já lavei.
entries.replyEn: Yes, I already did.

entries.pt: A que horas sais de casa?
entries.en: What time do you leave the house?
entries.replyPt: Saio por volta das nove menos um quarto.
entries.replyEn: I leave around a quarter to nine.

entries.pt: arrumar a cama antes de sair
entries.en: to make the bed before leaving

categories.blurbEn: The vocabulary for everyday mishaps — lost keys, broken gadgets, and the little surprises of daily life.

entries.note: mild exclamation of frustration, common and family-friendly

entries.en: By any chance... / As it happens...

entries.replyPt: Que chatice! Onde foi a última vez que as viste?
entries.replyEn: What a pain! Where did you last see them?

entries.replyPt: Fogo! Vamos ter de chamar o técnico.
entries.replyEn: Geez! We'll have to call the repairman.

entries.pt: Por acaso encontraste a minha carteira?
entries.en: Did you happen to find my wallet?
entries.replyPt: Ainda não, mas vou procurar.
entries.replyEn: Not yet, but I'll look for it.

entries.pt: Derramei café no sofá, sem querer.
entries.en: I spilled coffee on the sofa, by accident.
entries.replyPt: Não faz mal, ainda bem que não foi no tapete.
entries.replyEn: It's okay, at least it wasn't on the rug.

entries.en: We agreed to meet at three, remember?
entries.replyPt: Afinal já são quase quatro!
entries.replyEn: It's actually almost four already!

entries.pt: O telemóvel não está a funcionar.
entries.replyPt: Já reparaste se está carregado?
entries.replyEn: Have you checked if it's charged?
entries.note: o telemóvel — in Brazil: o celular

entries.pt: Preciso de devolver isto à loja.
entries.en: I need to return this to the store.
entries.replyPt: Podes reclamar e pedir o dinheiro de volta.
entries.replyEn: You can complain and ask for your money back.

entries.en: It suddenly started raining and I forgot my umbrella.
entries.replyPt: Que chatice! Vamos ter de esperar que passe.
entries.replyEn: What a pain! We'll have to wait for it to pass.

entries.pt: No fim, isto não vai dar em nada.
entries.en: In the end, this isn't going to amount to anything.
entries.replyPt: Calma, ainda há tempo para resolver.
entries.replyEn: Relax, there's still time to sort it out.

entries.en: I broke a glass by accident.
entries.replyPt: Não faz mal, eu limpo isso já.
entries.replyEn: It's okay, I'll clean it up right away.

entries.pt: voltar à loja para pedir a garantia
entries.en: to go back to the store to ask about the warranty
to complain without losing your cool

categories.blurbEn: Atlantic-coast weather and the four seasons, from fog and wind to sunny afternoons.

entries.note: common word along the coast for wave and surf reports

entries.en: to get colder / to cool down

entries.replyPt: Está vento e está fresco.
entries.replyEn: It's windy and cool.

entries.replyPt: Acho que sim, o céu está muito nublado.
entries.replyEn: I think so, the sky is very cloudy.

entries.replyPt: Pois está, deve levantar depois do almoço.
entries.replyEn: It sure is, it should clear up after lunch.

entries.replyPt: Está grande, boa para o surf.
entries.replyEn: It's big, good for surfing.

entries.pt: Qual é a tua estação preferida?
entries.replyPt: Prefiro o outono, não faz tanto calor.
entries.replyEn: I prefer fall, it's not as hot.

entries.replyPt: Está, mas não está a chover.
entries.replyEn: It is, but it's not raining.

entries.replyPt: Está, é melhor levar um casaco.
entries.replyEn: It is, you'd better bring a jacket.

entries.pt: Vai estar sol este fim de semana?
entries.en: Will it be sunny this weekend?
entries.replyPt: Acho que sim, parece que o tempo vai mudar.
entries.replyEn: I think so, it looks like the weather is going to change.

entries.pt: levar o casaco por causa do vento

categories.blurbEn: Getting around by bus, train, and car — plus asking for directions on the road.

entries.note: in Brazil: o ônibus
in Brazil: o trem
the iconic trams in Lisbon, like the famous number 28
in Brazil: dirigir

entries.replyPt: Vai até Torres Vedras, mas tens de mudar no centro.
entries.replyEn: It goes to Torres Vedras, but you have to change downtown.

entries.pt: A que horas parte o próximo comboio?
entries.en: What time does the next train leave?
entries.replyPt: Parte daqui a vinte minutos.
entries.replyEn: It leaves in twenty minutes.

entries.pt: Como se vai para a autoestrada daqui?
entries.en: How do you get to the highway from here?
entries.replyPt: Segue sempre em frente e depois vira à direita.
entries.replyEn: Keep going straight and then turn right.

entries.pt: Onde fica a estação de comboios?
entries.replyPt: Fica perto da rotunda, cinco minutos a pé.
entries.replyEn: It's near the roundabout, a five-minute walk.

entries.pt: Há muito trânsito na autoestrada hoje?
entries.en: Is there a lot of traffic on the highway today?
entries.replyPt: Há, principalmente perto da portagem.
entries.replyEn: There is, mostly near the toll.

entries.replyPt: Podes, mas só até às seis.
entries.replyEn: You can, but only until six.

entries.pt: Quanto custa a portagem até Lisboa?
entries.en: How much does the toll to Lisbon cost?
entries.replyPt: Custa uns cinco euros, mais ou menos.
entries.replyEn: It costs about five euros, more or less.

entries.pt: Vais de carro ou apanhas o comboio?
entries.en: Are you going by car or taking the train?
entries.replyPt: Vou de comboio, é mais calmo.
entries.replyEn: I'm taking the train, it's more relaxing.

entries.pt: encontrar um lugar para estacionar perto da estação
entries.en: to find a parking spot near the station

entries.pt: verificar os horários do comboio antes de sair de casa
entries.en: to check the train times before leaving the house

categories.blurbEn: Ordering coffee and food like a local, from a quick bica to a full prato do dia.

entries.note: in Porto often called um cimbalino; in Brazil, um cafezinho

entries.en: milky coffee served in a tall glass

entries.note: in Brazil: o cardápio
tipping isn't obligatory in Portugal; leaving small change is common and appreciated

entries.replyPt: Vou pedir o prato do dia.
entries.replyEn: I'm going to order the dish of the day.

entries.en: A galão and a toast, please.
entries.replyPt: Com certeza, mais alguma coisa?
entries.replyEn: Certainly, anything else?

entries.pt: Pode trazer a conta, por favor?
entries.en: Can you bring the bill, please?
entries.replyPt: Já lhe trago.
entries.replyEn: I'll bring it right away.

entries.pt: Queres uma bica ou um galão?
entries.en: Do you want a bica or a galão?
entries.replyPt: Prefiro uma bica, é mais forte.
entries.replyEn: I prefer a bica, it's stronger.

entries.pt: Qual é o prato do dia hoje?
entries.en: What's today's dish of the day?
entries.replyPt: Hoje é bacalhau com natas.
entries.replyEn: Today it's bacalhau com natas.

entries.replyPt: Aceitamos, sim.
entries.replyEn: Yes, we do.

entries.en: Do you think we should leave a tip?
entries.replyPt: Não é obrigatório, mas uns trocos são simpáticos.
entries.replyEn: It's not required, but some spare change is a nice gesture.

entries.pt: Está bom o vinho da casa?
entries.replyPt: Está, e não é caro.

entries.replyEn: Because it turns out I don't work tomorrow.

entries.replyEn: I am, let's eat something.
